gaps.sentence: That's exactly ___ I needed — thank you!
gaps.explanation: 'What I needed' means 'the thing that I needed'; 'that' cannot be used in this free relative position.

gaps.sentence: We arrived at the hotel at noon, ___ the rooms were not ready.
gaps.explanation: 'When' introduces non-defining clauses about time after a comma; 'that' is impossible after a comma.

gaps.sentence: Anyone ___ wants to join the trip should sign up today.
gaps.explanation: 'Anyone who' is the standard pattern; 'who' is the subject pronoun for people.

gaps.sentence: My uncle, ___ lives in Canada, is coming to stay next week.
gaps.hint: non-defining clause after a comma about a person
gaps.explanation: In non-defining clauses (between commas) 'that' is not allowed; 'who' refers to people.

gaps.sentence: It is one of the most impressive buildings ___ I have ever seen.
gaps.explanation: After superlative expressions, 'that' is the standard relative pronoun in defining clauses.

gaps.sentence: The director, ___ we met at the conference, has written to us.
gaps.hint: person as object, but the clause is non-defining
gaps.explanation: In non-defining clauses 'that' cannot replace 'who', even when the person is the object.

gaps.sentence: The Eiffel Tower, ___ attracts millions of visitors, was completed in 1889.
gaps.explanation: For things in non-defining clauses use 'which'; 'that' is not allowed after a comma.

gaps.sentence: I'll never forget the day ___ we first met.
gaps.explanation: 'When' replaces 'on which' after time nouns like day, year and moment.
